utterances.text: And between the corridor where have you been in the big room where the meeting took place is there a door? Is there an entrance? Is there a curtain? How did it look like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a direct entrance from that corridor where I was, but they divided that big room with partitions, and there were beds for the three men who slept there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have explained that, but you are not answering my question. I have another question. Were you the only guard at that moment, or were there other guards as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was one more who took turns with me, as I said in the beginning. Let me not mention his name again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... was this guard present during that meeting as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. There was always only one guard. I am only talking about what I heard. And if Office of the Prosecutor should ask the second guard about my story, God knows what he heard when he was on duty. This way, you get only half the picture from what I can recount.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I understand that. You have answered my question. My last question is: How long did this meeting last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An hour at most. It's difficult to say now. It was all prepared beforehand. It couldn't have lasted more than an hour, but it's really difficult for me to say 20 years later exactly. But as the discussion went, it couldn't have lasted more than an hour, an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You say it was all prepared beforehand. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They got the assignment to organise it, to decide how best to carry out that mortar - what shall I call it? - mortar attack. They had prepared it in advance, and they just came to tell Alija and Reis what they were going to do. These two heard them out and said, All right. Go ahead and do it properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And at the beginning you said Izetbegovic was first reluctant to accept the proposal by Reis. Was that the beginning of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. It's before all these discussions, when intersections began to be used as targets, when more casualties were caused than necessary, before all these events, when people were stopped at intersections -- but when one thing after another started, there was less and less resistance all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The proposal with respect to Markale made by Reis was not during this meeting, or was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the beginning, when they were discussing the whole strategy of it, when it was discussed that there and especially in the protected areas, such as Srebrenica, a more massive massacre should be caused for the international community to intervene, then, in the early days, Alija had doubts. But when things started running their course and when Markale was suggested, he agreed -- he didn't have any problem anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That means -- let me just clarify that. At least two meetings took place. One meeting between Izetbegovic and one with -- and with Reis and the other one including the other persons you have mentioned; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There could have been ten, but I was present only to what I told you. I can only tell you what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How many of these meetings where this was discussed have you observed or heard personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Who was present during the first meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Always the same people. Always the same people. They decided everything, and they carried out everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- follow-up questions. Sir, you indicated that Halilovic and Talijan implemented this idea. Were you present when they did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not, but I was present when they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you've answered my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I haven't. You can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... were you present when they implemented the plan. You say you were not. Listen to my next question. How do you know that they did implement that plan and that it was them who did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, that's something different. I was present when Alija approved their plan and its execution, Alija and Reis. They always spoke with one voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Moloto, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have explained that, and I've heard that. I'm now taking a step further. I'm asking you how you came to know that Halilovic and Talijan did, in fact, implement the task, the idea, because you say you were not there when they did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second meeting, when it happened, it was all within seven days, at most. They came to say that they had tried but it didn't work. Perhaps they miscalculated, so the shell fell on a roof near the Markale market. They missed only by 2 metres --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... can I stop you, please. You're now telling me of a meeting when they came to report. I'm asking you about when the plan that was being implemented. How did you know that, in fact, they did implement the plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to tell you this. They organised a second meeting where I was present and they explained to Reis and to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I appreciate what you want to tell me but please answer my question first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- what's wrong with this microphone? How did you know that it was Halilovic and Talijan who implemented this plan? You say you were not there with them when they did it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Alija sent them. That meeting finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you are obviously not answering my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to tell you there was another meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They came to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about another meeting. I'm asking you about the implementation of the plan. And I'm just wanting -- you can tell me about the meeting later, but that's not what I'm asking you. I'd just like to know if you were not present when the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's how they knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... about how people knew. I'm asking you how you know that it was Halilovic and Talijan who implemented the plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you deliberately trying to confuse me? I'm telling you quite clearly. If you let me speak, it will be clear. But if you deliberately interrupt me, I can't tell you anything. Please listen to me at least for once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's try again. Tell me, in your own words, how you do know that Halilovic and Talijan implemented this plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the first meeting, everything was arranged; Alija authorised it and left. On the second meeting -- at the second meeting, Talijan returned, as well as Sefer Halilovic, to submit a report to Alija; and they gave him reasons for which they were unsuccessful for which the shell had missed. There were three meetings. I heard them submitting a report, and that is an answer to your previous question. They came to explain the reasons for which they hadn't succeeded. Alija said, Try again. That was the agreement. And then they said that they would have to wait for that UNPROFOR position with that vehicle and they then left, and that was the end of the story. Later we all heard about what happened at Markale, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I -- if I understand you well, you were present when there was a report about the failed attempt, but you concluded that they had implemented the plan when you heard about a successful mortar round hitting the Markale market?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard about it and I saw it. As to who is responsible, you will have to draw your own conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was there any further report in a meeting with Izetbegovic once the market was hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Even if there was meeting, it was probably held when the other guard was present, so that -- I don't know that Markale was subsequently discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one small question, a detail again about the corridor of 3 metres long. If you would come from the garage, go through that corridor of 3 metres long, was there a door when entering the large room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a door only in the external wall, the main external wall. This wasn't really a garage. It was a sort of a makeshift garage, sort of makeshift roof had been erected over those luxury cars. Do you understand what I'm saying? I don't know how to explain what this gate looked like. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wanted to know whether you could move, walking from the garage - makeshift or not - into that room without going through a door; or was there a door between where the cars were parked and where the room was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a door in the external wall, a reinforced metal door, because it was a bank and you know the kind of doors they have. But there was this corridor then, and then there were no more doors and you would suddenly enter the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where you were seated, was that before that door you had you to go through to the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Behind. It was linked to this room, and that is where I sat on the first two occasions. I spent two shifts on the outside, and then the shelling in the vicinity intensified, so Alija said, Don't stay out there, come inside, it's safer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what you told us before. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll now move onto the next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the commander of the 28th Division of the ABiH, Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever meet Mr. Oric in the room for which you provided security for Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you can remember, how many times did Naser Oric go to the room we have mentioned?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: I know of three times. On one occasion, I went to fetch him in Dobrinje. I took him to the Holiday Inn; he stayed there, slept over. And then on the following day, I took him from the Holiday Inn to the central bank building. I know that he came on two other occasions. That's when I saw him. As for the other occasions on which he came, I don't know. But on the other occasions, I didn't escort him. I escorted him there only on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you personally have the opportunity of hearing the conversation held between Mr. Oric and Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the two of them discussed and whether anyone else was present at those discussions.

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Well, Reis was always there, Sefer was always there, and Talijan. And these two men were also always there, but they never participated in the discussions. I'm referring to Jasmin and Bakir. They only listened to what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the subject of those discussions that you heard?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: They were always discussing Srebrenica, the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They said that this situation was in no way acceptable for us, that a way had to be found to make the international community intervene and to intervene militarily to put an end to the situation. Naser was ordered to create some disorder down there, to provoke the Serbs to intensify their shelling, and the purpose of all of this was to provoke an international intervention. That is what was considered to be imperative because we weren't having any military success, so everything was being done to provoke a military intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of incidents are you referring to? What sort of incidents was the command of the 28th Division supposed to provoke?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Well, he was given the task to form groups of three or four men who could always get through the roadblocks, and he was to create as much chaos as possible in the Serbian villages, to anger the Serbs, and make them shell Srebrenica. Since Srebrenica was a safe haven, that would mean that these people would have to get involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask you one clarifying question. You said you were aware of three occasions where Mr. Oric met with Mr. Izetbegovic. You said only one of them you attended. But you also told us "they were always discussing Srebrenica." Could you explain to me how you could tell us that that's what they always did if you are, at the same time, telling us that you were only once present during such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a mistake, either mine or yours. I was at the meeting three times. But I only escorted him only on one occasion from Dobrinja, but I was present at the three meetings. As to whether there were other meetings, I don't know. I also -- I was also present when discussions were held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said: "As for the other occasions on which he came, I don't know." And indeed you said you escorted --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apart from those three occasions. If there were any other occasions -- I know about three occasions, but I don't know about any other occasions apart from those three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During those three meetings that you attended, did they discuss the fact that incidents such as the ones you have described actually occurred in the field around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Stojanovic, would you please rephrase. But is there -- is there dispute about the fact that sometimes actions were taken from the Srebrenica area and surrounding Serb-held territory?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, but that's not the concern. It's whether the witness's recollection and leading the witness's recollection on to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that point. But it's of no use to discuss it anyhow if there's no dispute about the matter that this sometimes happened. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic and keep both in mind, both about the leading and when there's no dispute that sometimes such actions were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we're discussing whether -- not whether the incidents happened but whether, according to the orders -- but we're discussing the orders that came from those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, at the three meetings that you attended, did Mr. Oric report to Mr. Izetbegovic about what was happening in relation to these incidents in Srebrenica and around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: He didn't really submit many reports about that, but when he was last there, when he received a direct order on the last occasion he was there, not before that, he didn't really receive any orders and didn't have to give reports. He just spoke about the general situation in Srebrenica and about what was happening. But on the last occasion, on the third occasion, when he received a direct order to form groups of three men who would infiltrate Serbian territory, well, after a certain period of time I heard how they were saying that Naser was doing his work very well. That's all. As to what that meant, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And before the break, I just have one more subject to deal with. When performing your duties, in the course of your duties, did you ever provide security for any of the presidents for the neighbouring countries?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Yes, for Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court something about this, but just briefly. Could you tell the Court what exactly you did and what you saw.

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Well, there was a war between us and the Croats which was ongoing. I believe that they had gone for a walk in a little park in front of the Presidency, and Reis said that we had to make peace with someone, that we won't wage war on so many sides because a war was being waged again the Croats and against the Serbs and against local criminals Baboj [phoen] and Velika Kladusa. He said we can't put up such resistance, we can't fight a war against everyone. We have to make peace with someone. We can't make peace with the Serbs because in military terms the Serbs were doing well, so it wouldn't be possible to make peace with them; they wouldn't want to. And so we had to make peace with the Croats. And there was one good thing. He said, "We've got two pieces of shit and we have to bite into at least one piece." So they decided to make the peace with the Croats and I think Sacir --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreter heard the name correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- helped them. Alija used him to ask Tudjman to come to Sarajevo through the intermediary of the Americans. They listened to him and ten days later Tudjman came to Sarajevo although he was a terrible criminal for most of the people in Sarajevo because there had been quite a lot of victims in Mostar and so on and so forth. We called Croats around the cathedral to welcome him. There was some other people from our community. So when Tudjman came out, he thought he would receive -- he wouldn't be well received, but they chanted his name and he was nicely surprised. That improved his mood. And he went to see Alija. They had a meeting and Tudjman probably liked the role of a peacemaker. The peace agreement was soon signed. If you need me to go into further detail, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll stop now. It's time for a break, and then I will put a few more questions to you after the break, after which we will conclude my examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the curtains be pulled down. We take a break, Witness, and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. Mr. Stojanovic, as far as timing is concerned, could you tell us where we are?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have one more subject to deal with. I have three or, rather, four documents. I don't think I will need more than 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll have those 15 minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I think I won't be using up more time than I had requested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you would not, if you would -- certainly not. We take a break, and we resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the curtains be drawn up again. Before I give an opportunity to Mr. Stojanovic to continue, I've one short question, and please try to keep your answer short as well. We discussed before the break this meeting where six persons were present, where Mr. Izetbegovic had approved plans by Sefer Halilovic and Talijan to develop a -- an incident, a serious incident, in order to provoke the international community to take action. Now, was Mr. Ceric present at that meeting when Izetbegovic approved it or was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was. And I know that because Alija's two relatives and Ceric had come from the Presidency together and there were the two of them waiting there, so I know that's why he was there too. Throughout that time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand your answer. But earlier we discussed those present and you didn't mention him. So would you please Ive accurate in your answer, because now you add a seventh person. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think there's a misunderstanding as to whether he was mentioned or not. He wasn't mentioned personally but in terms of his function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- you're not supposed to give evidence. It wasn't mentioned as such. If you want to draw your attention to things I may have overlooked, then please give me the page and the line number and then I'll seriously look at it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And please put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in the previous session, you testified about how many people were present in response to a question put to you by the Court. My question will be a direct one now. Did you mention the function, the function of the person you call Reis?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember whether I said that Reis -- whether I mentioned the name, that he was there. In any event, if there's a mistake, it can be corrected. Reis Afendija, Mustafa Ceric did attend the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript page 57, lines 10 to 12 of today's hearing. With your leave, I will move on to the following question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. This certainly was helpful, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, while you were performing the duties that you have described, did you have the opportunity to leave the town of Sarajevo? Did you have that possibility?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Yes, and I took advantage of such opportunities on three occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court where you went on these three occasions when you left the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us how you managed to leave the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Well, I have an UNPROFOR card, or I had an UNPROFOR card. That was also the case for certain other individuals in the Presidency, although not for many, and with such a card we had the right once every three months to take advantage of an UNPROFOR flight to Ancona or to Frankfurt. It depended on what was available. I took advantage of that right on three occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how you crossed the demarcation line between the warring factions in Sarajevo on those three occasions?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Well, since the card I had was an UNPROFOR card, and I wasn't always alone, I was in a group of individuals who were using these cards, they usually have -- a personnel carrier would pick these people up, take them to the airport in Sarajevo. We would wait for a transport plane, a cargo plane; those are the planes that were usually used. They would unload the goods they had brought to Sarajevo and then would return to Ancona or Frankfurt. I flew to Frankfurt twice and once to Ancona because that was the last flight, there wasn't going to be another one for a week. So I said, I'll go to Ancona, and then I drove on from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, did you ever use the tunnel below the airport to get out?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have the opportunity of personally seeing any military equipment and weapons being transported to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Well, there's nothing secret about this. Whatever was transported there -- well, I mean, the tunnel was made for those purposes. That was the only purpose of that tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After the visit of Mr. Tudjman to Sarajevo that you discussed before the break, did you notice a different, more intensive delivery of weapons?

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Weapons began to arrive more regularly, and even before that, it was said that we have enough weapons over there in Split.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The question was leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The previous one as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What should we do to remind you of avoiding such leading questions, Mr. Stojanovic? I think we're ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will mind your instruction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You started saying something, Witness.

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: Can I speak freely in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you wish for a private session, we can organise it.

utterances.speaker: GRM116
utterances.text: I have to explain how the weapons came in and then I have to mention Germany and names and humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, could we now go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What the witness told us is not a reason to go into private session. You can -- as long as it doesn't reveal your identity, you can speak freely about Germany or whatever, humanitarian aid, names in Germany, everything is fine as long as it does not reveal your identity. So please tell us whether you would continue in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just ask. (redacted) (redacted) Now if I have to mention -- in fact, the Prosecutor reacted. Now I have to mention it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Witness, we'll resume tomorrow, because now we'll adjourn for this day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 where we expect to be able to conclude your testimony. You'll then be cross-examined. For the Registry, the next -- we're resuming with the next -- with the witness who started earlier his testimony certainly will not take place in the first and perhaps not even in the second session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do expect to be under my time estimate, so it's possible in the second session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, that witness should remain on standby during the second session. Witness, before we adjourn, I want to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that's testimony you've given today or whether it's testimony still to be given tomorrow. Once the curtains are down, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for counsel having assisted the witness, the same instruction for you: That you should not speak or communicate in any way with whomever, including your client, to discuss or communicate in whatever way about this testimony. You may follow the usher. We'll adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 16th of December, 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise. When I said "this same courtroom, I," I made a mistake, because tomorrow we'll be in Courtroom II -- III. Well, it's not easy to count to three for a man with moderate intellectual capacities. Let's adjourn, and we'll see you back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of December, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.19 p.m.,
